growth.label: Revenue growth
growth.rationale: ANALYST OVERRIDE: Q1 FY27 revenue +23% came from product mix while four-wheeler units fell 11.8% y/y; CBU import duties were cut from July 2026 and the Auto Policy 2026-31 is pending, slowing NEV bookings; three-wheeler units +44.7%. FY27E 12%, FY28E 15% as new capacity (54,000 units p.a. single shift) and models ramp, fading to 7% nominal PKR by FY33E. Historical 3y CAGR (119%) reflects a launch-cycle step change and is not extrapolated [EV-0010, EV-0004]. (Rule-based value replaced: Year 1 anchored on reported year-to-date growth of 23.3% vs prior-year period; then fading linearly from the run-rate 25.0% to 5.5% by the final year (terminal growth 5.0%). Historical 3y CAGR 119.3%, 5y CAGR 116.5%. Historical run-rate 105.9% capped at 25.0% (sector playbook: cyclical business; recent growth not extrapolated).)

ebit_margin.label: EBIT margin
ebit_margin.rationale: ANALYST OVERRIDE: Starts near the Q1 FY27 operating margin (14.7%) after the company absorbed the hybrid sales-tax increase (8.5%/12.75% to 18%); fades to 12.5% as new entrants, NEV competition and lower tariff protection (CBU duty cuts) erode pricing. FY25 (23.6%) and FY26 (19.0%) margins are treated as cyclical peaks [EV-0010, EV-0005]. (Rule-based value replaced: Starts at YTD margin 14.7%; fades halfway to the 5y average 15.2% by the final year (mean reversion absent evidence of structural change).)

tax_rate.label: Effective tax rate
tax_rate.rationale: 3y median effective rate 38.9% (bounded to statutory 39.0% +/-10pp), converging to the midpoint with statutory (39.0%) as a prudence assumption on global minimum-tax and rate risk. Statutory rate source: annual report p.244: 'corporation tax rate of 29% (2025: 29%) and super tax at 10%' [EV-0002].

capex_pct.label: Capex / revenue
capex_pct.rationale: ANALYST OVERRIDE: A new expansion plan with an estimated budget of PKR 22.0bn (paint shop, civil works, ancillary equipment) was approved after completing the PKR 11.5bn four-wheeler expansion; spend assumed over FY27-FY28 (about 5% of revenue), then maintenance capex of about 2% of revenue [EV-0004]. (Rule-based value replaced: Held at the 3y average 5.8%.)

dna_pct.label: D&A / revenue
dna_pct.rationale: ANALYST OVERRIDE: Depreciation was 0.29% of FY26 revenue on a much smaller asset base; it rises as the completed and approved expansions (about PKR 33bn) are capitalised, converging below maintenance capex (<= 90% of capex) by FY33E [EV-0004]. (Rule-based value replaced: 3y average 0.3% converging to <= 90% of capex (0.3%) so a growing business keeps net investment positive.)

nwc_pct.label: Operating NWC / revenue
nwc_pct.rationale: Held at the 3y average 3.0%; a negative value means suppliers/customers fund operations.

buyback_pct.label: Buybacks (% of FCF after dividends)
buyback_pct.rationale: Historical buybacks were n/a of net income (3y avg); modelled as 0.0% of free cash flow after dividends (capped at 100%). Buybacks at expected market prices are value-neutral in the DCF; they affect forecast EPS and net cash only.

synthesis.headline: Priced for a collapse in local assembly: at PKR 1,394.80 the market implies shrinking sales; we value SAZEW at PKR 1,102-3,318 (central PKR 2,289, probability-weighted PKR 2,239), but the Auto Policy 2026-31 outcome is close to binary
executive_summary: Sazgar has become a scaled four-wheeler assembler for GWM (Haval, Tank, ORA) and BAIC on top of its three-wheeler franchise: FY26 revenue was PKR 191,715m (+76.4%) and net profit PKR 23,605m, EPS 390.51 [EV-0002, EV-0027].

The share trades at 3.6x trailing earnings with net cash of about PKR 10.2bn at 30 September 2026 [EV-0001, EV-0003]. Reverse DCF: holding our margins, the price requires revenue to shrink about 2.0% a year for seven years, or EBIT margins of about 9.0% against 13.7% in our base case.

Our base case (revenue +12% in FY27E, EBIT margin fading from 15.0% to 12.5%, 21.5% cost of equity in PKR) gives a DCF value of PKR 2,268 and a reliability-weighted fair value of PKR 2,289; the bear and bull cases span PKR 1,102 to PKR 3,318 (interpretation: the margin of safety exists even in the bear case, but not in the policy-stress case of PKR 559).

The near-term trend is weakening, not improving: Q1 FY27 four-wheeler units fell 11.81% while three-wheelers rose 44.69%, and the company absorbed the sales-tax rise on hybrids, cutting operating profit to PKR 6,148m from PKR 6,809m [EV-0010, EV-0003].

The decisive variable is policy: customs duties on imported CBU vehicles were reduced from July 2026 and the Auto Policy 2026-31 was still pending at quarter end; management itself warns of declining local production without an adequate tariff differential [EV-0010].

thesis_pillars.title: The price discounts a structural collapse that the evidence does not (yet) show
thesis_pillars.argument: At 3.6x trailing earnings the market requires about -2.0% annual revenue decline or a 9.0% EBIT margin to justify the price. Q1 FY27 revenue still grew to PKR 41,711m from PKR 33,825m and the order book shifted towards higher-value models (favourable mix) [EV-0010]. Our base case already haircuts margins from 19.0% (FY26) to 12.5% (interpretation).

thesis_pillars.title: Capacity, product pipeline and balance sheet give room to absorb a downturn
thesis_pillars.argument: The PKR 11.50bn four-wheeler expansion is complete (capacity 54,000 units a year on a single shift) and a further PKR 22.00bn plan (fully automatic paint shop) was approved; new CKD PHEV/HEV models (Haval H6 PHEV, Tank 500 PHEV and HEV) were launched [EV-0004, EV-0027]. Cash of PKR 18,041m against debt of about PKR 7.8bn at 30 September 2026 and an A+ credit rating (VIS) reduce financing risk [EV-0003, EV-0027].

thesis_pillars.title: Three-wheelers are a cash-generative hedge against the car cycle
thesis_pillars.argument: Three-wheeler units rose 44.69% in Q1 FY27 and revenue from the segment rose to PKR 3,135.79m from PKR 2,017.87m; management expects the segment to remain an important contributor, with exports being pursued (Japan among markets) [EV-0010, EV-0004]. It is small (about 8% of Q1 sales) so it cushions rather than offsets a four-wheeler downturn (interpretation).

synthesis.priced_in: The reverse DCF on the same model shows the PKR 1,394.80 price is consistent with revenue falling about 2.0% a year over seven years at our margins, or with an average EBIT margin of about 9.0% at our growth (base case 13.7%). Peers on the PSX trade at a median 6.1x trailing P/E versus about 3.6x for SAZEW [EV-0021, EV-0022, EV-0024, EV-0025, EV-0001]. The market is therefore pricing a sharp loss of competitiveness for locally assembled vehicles (interpretation), consistent with the CBU duty cuts and the pending Auto Policy flagged by management [EV-0010]. Caveat on the cross-check: the comparables value (median P/E 6.1x applied to trailing net profit of PKR 23,223m) uses near-peak earnings, so it embeds cyclical optimism; on normalised earnings it would be lower, and it is used only as a cross-check (30% methodology weight).
synthesis.variant_perception: We agree the FY25-FY26 margins (23.6% and 19.0% EBIT) were cyclical peaks and build in further compression to 12.5%. Where we differ is on volume: the evidence shows a mix-driven revenue increase in Q1 FY27, completed capacity, new PHEV/HEV CKD models and a growing three-wheeler business [EV-0010, EV-0027, EV-0004], whereas the price implies outright shrinkage. Our view is an interpretation of policy outcomes that are not yet known; if the Auto Policy materially narrows the tariff differential the market will be right (see stress case).
synthesis.business_analysis: Sazgar assembles and markets four-wheelers under Chinese brands BAIC and GWM (Haval, Tank, ORA) through 20+ four-wheeler dealers, three-wheelers (auto-rickshaws, petrol and EV variants) under the SAZGAR brand through 50+ booking agents, and automotive parts (tractor wheel rims mainly for Millat Tractors and Al-Ghazi Tractors) [EV-0027, EV-0004]. No customer exceeds 10% of sales and exports were only PKR 78.34m in FY26 [EV-0027]. The home-appliances business was discontinued from 1 September 2025 [EV-0004]. Revenue is almost entirely domestic and four-wheelers were PKR 38,443.07m of PKR 41,711m Q1 FY27 sales, so the company is effectively a single-country, single-segment cyclical [EV-0010]. Customer advances are a key funding source: trade and other payables were PKR 28,193m at 30 September 2026, against stock-in-trade of PKR 41,771m [EV-0003] - a sudden slowdown in bookings would reverse this funding (interpretation).
synthesis.industry_analysis: Industry volumes are recovering: auto sector sales rose 27.71% in Q1 FY27 and four-wheelers (excluding tractors) 20.57% (source cited by the company: RAMA) [EV-0010]. Sazgar's four-wheeler units nevertheless fell 11.81%, implying share loss in the quarter (interpretation), which management links to delayed Auto Policy finalisation hitting NEV bookings [EV-0010]. Competition is intensifying with new manufacturers, expansion of existing assemblers and the shift to NEVs [EV-0005]. Key input exposures are CKD kit availability and prices, and PKR depreciation; the annual report quantifies the sensitivity of pre-tax profit to a 1% PKR move on foreign-currency balances (financial risk note) [EV-0007, EV-0002].
synthesis.financial_assessment: Growth has been exceptional but cash conversion poor. Revenue grew from PKR 4,034m (FY21) to PKR 191,715m (FY26) and EBIT margin from 2.7% to 19.0% [EV-0002]. However operating cash flow fell to PKR 9,598m in FY26 from PKR 14,115m as inventory rose to PKR 42,068m and tax payments increased; the 3-year average FCF/net income is only 0.19x and the accruals ratio is 22.7% (computed flags). Capex of PKR 15,637m in FY26 funded the expansion, partly with new diminishing musharakah financing (PKR 5.2bn) [EV-0002, EV-0004]. The balance sheet reconciles in every year (FY21-FY26) and the platform resolved one OCR conflict in the audited profit and loss account (finance cost) using accounting identities (see discrepancy log). Tax is a heavy 39% (29% corporate plus 10% super tax) [EV-0002].
synthesis.forecast_rationale: Revenue +12% in FY27E (Q1 +23% on mix but four-wheeler units -11.81%), +15% in FY28E as new capacity and models ramp, fading to 7% nominal PKR by FY33E; EBIT margin from 15.0% to 12.5% to reflect competition and tariff erosion; capex at about 5% of revenue for FY27E-FY28E for the PKR 22.00bn plan, then about 2%; depreciation rising from 0.45% to 1.7% of revenue as the expansions are capitalised; tax 39%. All are labelled analyst assumptions with evidence ids in the workbook [EV-0010, EV-0004, EV-0005].
synthesis.governance_capital_allocation: Free float is 35% (21,156,087 shares) [EV-0001], so control rests with the sponsors; the CEO (Mian Asad Hameed), the chairperson (Mrs. Saira Asad Hameed) and the COO of the car division (Mian Muhammad Ali Hameed) share the family name [EV-0027] - a related-party and succession question we could not test further (evidence gap: pattern of shareholding and related-party note not analysed). Dividends rose to PKR 70 per share for FY26 (payout about 18%) and an interim PKR 5 was declared for Q1 FY27 [EV-0002, EV-0010]. Capital allocation is mostly reinvestment in capacity, but the purchase of two commercial plots in Lahore (Pine Avenue and CBD) is non-core and warrants scrutiny [EV-0027].

counter_thesis.argument: SAZEW's earnings are a policy artefact: CKD assemblers enjoyed a protected market, and with CBU duties cut from July 2026 and an Auto Policy that may further reduce protection, imported vehicles and new Chinese entrants could compress local volumes and margins far below our base case. Q1 FY27 already shows four-wheeler units -11.81%, margin pressure from absorbed taxes, weak cash conversion (FCF/net income 0.19x) and an inventory of PKR 41,771m that could need discounting. On this view peak-cycle earnings deserve a 3-4x multiple and the stock is fairly priced or expensive. The early warning is already visible: in Q1 FY27 trade and other payables (largely customer advances) fell to PKR 28,193m from PKR 30,722m while stock-in-trade stayed at PKR 41,771m, and trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow turned negative (PKR -1,584m) [EV-0003].
counter_thesis.evaluation: The counter-thesis is credible and is the main reason confidence is only MEDIUM. Evidence supports parts of it: unit decline, tax absorption, shrinking customer advances against a flat inventory and negative trailing operating cash flow [EV-0010, EV-0003], plus management's own warning about local production [EV-0010]. Against it: revenue still grew in Q1, the company holds net cash of about PKR 10.2bn, carries an A+ rating and has new PHEV/HEV CKD models [EV-0027, EV-0003], and our base case already assumes margins well below FY26. The working-capital evidence lowers our confidence in FY27E cash flow but not the base-case value materially, because the DCF already includes PKR 6bn+ of NWC build over the horizon (interpretation). The stress case (growth -25pp for two years, margin -8pp) gives PKR 559 and quantifies the downside if the counter-thesis proves right.

synthesis.upside_requirements: Upside to our PKR 2,268-3,318 range requires an Auto Policy that preserves a meaningful CKD/CBU tariff differential, recovery in four-wheeler units with the new PHEV/HEV models, margins holding near 15% rather than falling to the 9% the price implies, and a normalisation of working capital as the expansion completes [EV-0010, EV-0027].
synthesis.downside_triggers: A policy that sharply narrows tariff protection, continued four-wheeler unit declines while the industry grows, further absorbed taxes, or an inventory write-down. Our bear case (growth -8pp, margin -4pp, WACC +0.5pp) gives PKR 1,102 and the stress case PKR 559.
falsification: Auto Policy 2026-31 cuts the CKD/CBU tariff differential materially and monthly four-wheeler units fall more than 25% year on year for two consecutive quarters.
EBIT margin below 10% for two consecutive quarters without a one-off explanation.
Operating cash flow negative for FY27 while capex stays above PKR 10bn, forcing new borrowing or a dividend cut.
dominant_assumptions: EBIT margin path (base 15.0% to 12.5%): each 1pp shift in every year moves value by about 8% (engine margin x growth grid: PKR 2,084 to PKR 2,452 for -1pp/+1pp).
Revenue growth path, which depends on the Auto Policy outcome: each 1pp in every year moves value by about 4% (PKR 2,177 to PKR 2,364).
Cost of equity of 21.5% (including the 9.71% Pakistan country risk premium) and the 5.0% nominal PKR terminal growth assumption; terminal value is 42% of EV.
Whether trailing earnings are a cyclical peak: the comparables cross-check is on trailing (near-peak) earnings.
evidence_gaps: No dated Auto Policy 2026-31 text or tariff schedule was retrieved; the policy outcome is unknown.
No monthly industry (PAMA) or company unit series was analysed beyond the Q1 FY27 report; the retrieved monthly production/sales disclosures were image PDFs without extractable text.
Pattern of shareholding, related-party transactions and remuneration were not analysed.
No sourced broker consensus for PSX autos was accessible; none is used.
Price history from PSX is not available to non-browser clients, so beta is bottom-up (Damodaran EM Auto & Truck) rather than a regression.
Country risk data (Damodaran) is dated 5 January 2026.
synthesis.confidence_rationale: Historical financials are audited, cross-checked between documents and reconcile; cost-of-capital inputs are sourced and dated. Confidence is limited by a near-binary policy decision, a weakening Q1 trend in four-wheelers, poor cash conversion and the evidence gaps listed.

playbook.description: Pakistan automobile assemblers (CKD assembly of cars/SUVs, light commercial, two/three-wheelers). Imported kits priced in USD/JPY/CNY, sold in PKR; demand driven by policy rates, auto financing, prices and tariffs.
key_questions: Volume outlook by segment (four-wheelers vs three-wheelers): what drove the latest units trend and is it cyclical or structural?
Pricing power vs PKR depreciation and taxes: can price increases pass through kit costs and sales-tax changes without losing volume?
Policy: Auto Policy 2026-31, CBU import duty cuts, NEV/hybrid incentives and sales-tax treatment
Competitive intensity from new Chinese/Korean entrants and CBU imports
Capacity expansion: return on the new investment and funding
Customer advances and inventory: working-capital swing risk if bookings slow

exposures.factor: Tariff and auto-policy changes (CBU duty cuts, Auto Policy 2026-31)
exposures.transmission: lower CBU duties / less tariff protection -> imported vehicles cheaper relative to local CKD -> lower local volumes and pricing -> revenue and gross margin -> FCFF and terminal value
higher sales tax absorbed by company -> lower net price -> gross margin
weaker PKR -> higher CKD kit cost in PKR -> gross margin until price increases pass through -> EBIT
higher policy rate / tighter auto-finance rules -> lower financed purchases -> volumes; also higher discount rate
new models and price competition -> market share and price discounts -> volume and margin
LC restrictions -> kit shortages -> production stoppages -> volumes and fixed-cost absorption
slower bookings -> lower advances, higher inventory -> working-capital outflow -> FCFF
GDP/consumer slowdown -> lower volumes -> revenue and operating leverage -> lower FCFF
higher real rates -> higher discount rate -> lower PV of long-duration cash flows
stronger reporting currency -> lower translated foreign revenue -> revenue growth
